page.layout: One column of running text, set in roman and italic, with no marginal notes. Below the last line, at the right, one Greek catchword. The left edge shows only the neighbouring page's edge and show-through, which are left out.

main_text.p: & anathemati subjicerent. Nec id solum, sed quam horrenda sibi deprecarentur, si quid ex iam dictis placitis immutassent, & Photium hoc modo depositum uti Antistitem quomodocunque accepissent. Tum postmodum elapso tempore valida hac invertentes, & publicis congressibus rursus in Ecclesia testae instar transmutata publice pradicantes, vociferantes, plaudentes, & prolixis laudibus, atque encomiis Photium extollentes, & coronantes, hominem Dei verum enunciantes, legitimum Antistitem, Canonicam Ecclesiae lampadem, orbis terrarum lumen, pietatis assertorem, veritatis magistrum. Episcopi hi Photium deponunt, excommunicant, horrenda sibi, si illum remiserint, deprecantur. Ignatius illis ab excommunicatione, & anathemate immunis est. neque spondent nunquam se eum in posterum receptunext ros. Et Photiani dicunt semper Photio Orientales adhaesisse, & uti Patriarcham recognovisse? Diris, quibus se devoverant, affligentur.

Actione tertia damnantur Synodi Nicolai, Adriani, & Octava generalis, in quibus Photius de multis sceleribus convictus, & quod tyrannice pulso legitimo pastore thronum occupasset, deijcitur & condemnatur. Videtur sumpta occasio ex Commonitorio Joannis Pontificis; Θίλω-

page.notes: The first paragraph continues from the previous page. The final Greek word breaks at the line end (Θίλω-) and is completed in the catchword; the catchword reading is doubtful. The Greek line is hard to read and is marked [?]. The sentence "neque spondent nunquam se eum in posterum receptu-ros" is hyphenated across lines in the printed text and was joined without a space. Spelling of "deijcitur", "recognovisse" and "receptu-ros" follows the print. Long s was rendered as s throughout. Left-margin marks are show-through or the neighbouring page's edge and are not transcribed.
